sentences.text:
(At present undergoing imprisonment in District Jail Kishangarhbas, Alwar).
 ----Petitioner  Versus State of Rajasthan Through P.P.
 ----Respondent __________________________________________ For Petitioner : Mr. Govind Sharma For Respondent : Mr. Ram Ratan Gurjar, P.P.
__________________________________________  HON'BLE MRS. JUSTICE SABINA  Order 16/01/2018  Petitioner had faced trial qua offence punishable under Section 7/16 of the The Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as the 'Act').
 Trial court vide judgment/order dated 20.06.2003, ordered the conviction and sentence of the petitioner under Section 7/16 of Roshan Lal vs State on 16 January, 2018

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3263740/
1 the Act.
Appeal filed by the petitioner was dismissed by the Appellate Court vide order dated 04.09.2003.
Hence, the present petition by the petitioner.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner has already undergone about two and a half months of actual sentence.
Petitioner is facing the criminal proceedings since the year 1996.
Petitioner is the sole bread earner of his family and is not a previous convict.

Learned counsel has submitted that sentence qua imprisonment of the petitioner be reduced to the period already undergone by him and has not challenged the  (2 of 2)
conviction of the petitioner as ordered by the courts below.

In support of his arguments, learned counsel has placed reliance on the judgment of this court in Loonaram Vs. The State of Rajasthan WLN (UC) 1977, 571 and on the judgments of the Punjab and Haryana High Court in the case of Bharat Lal Vs. The State of Haryana 1993 (2) FAC Cases 65, Mahabir Parashad Vs. The State of Haryana 1993 (2) FAC Cases 83 and Anil Kumar Vs. State of Haryana 2015 (2) FAC 381.
 Learned state counsel, has opposed the submissions made by learned counsel for the petitioner.

Keeping in view the facts and circumstances of the case, it would be just and expedient to reduce the sentence qua imprisonment of the petitioner to the period already undergone by him and increase the sentence qua fine.
Accordingly, conviction of the petitioner under Section 7/16 of the Act, is maintained.

However,
sentence qua imprisonment of the petitioner is reduced to the period already undergone by him.
